target_customer: Pharma and biotech companies developing gene and cell therapies, plus academic partners
problem: Designing viral and non-viral delivery vehicles and genetic payloads for genomic medicines is slow and trial-and-error; WhiteLab uses machine learning to predict the best molecular designs before lab testing.
business_model: AI-enabled drug design: partnerships and collaborations with pharma plus an internal portfolio of validated bio-assets
product_category: TechBio, AI design of gene and cell therapy delivery vectors and payloads (ALFRED platform)

founders.name: David Delbourgo
education: MS biomedical engineering, University of Compiegne
founders.background_notes: YC page describes about 23 years in healthcare innovation. TechCrunch spells the name David Del Bourgo.

founders.name: Julien Cottineau
education: PhD genetics, molecular biology and immunology, Universite Pierre et Marie Curie
founders.background_notes: Senior application scientist at Genomic Vision per YC page; research fellow in J-L Casanova's lab.

competitors.name: BenevolentAI
competitors.what: AI drug discovery company named by TechCrunch as similar to WhiteLab

competitors.name: Cellino
competitors.what: AI-driven cell therapy manufacturing startup named by TechCrunch as similar

competitors.name: Dyno Therapeutics
competitors.what: Machine learning plus high throughput in vivo experiments to engineer AAV capsids (CapsidMap)
competitors.traction_then: partners listed on a profile include Novartis, Sarepta, Roche, Spark and Astellas (dates not shown)
competitors.funding_then: 100M Series A led by a16z in 2021

technical_complexity.rationale: Requires ML models trained on genetics knowledge graphs plus wet lab validation in vivo of viral and non-viral vectors; research-grade work with biology experiments.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary platform, knowledge graph from partner and proprietary datasets, and validated bio-assets, but well funded rivals such as Dyno existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition; the company kept raising (Series A 2022, Series B 2026) and partnered with Sanofi and Cytiva per its website.

market_need_then: Gene and cell therapy developers needed better vector and payload design; Dyno raised a 100M Series A in 2021, showing investor appetite for AI in this space.

branding.domain_note: Uses whitelabgx.com (abbreviated domain); history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and mission driven, collaborative, partner testimonials emphasise accelerated timelines.

branding.brand_signature: ALFRED, the platform name, an acronym for AI-Led Framework for Rational Exploration in Drug Design

brand_strength.rationale: Recognised by Station F Future 40 and YC but no brand-level press or community evidence; B2B science brand.

outcome_analysis: WhiteLab Genomics is Active and growing: it raised a 10M Series A in 2022 led by Omnes Capital and Debiopharm, then a 26M Series B in October 2026 led by AVP with both existing investors returning. Founders pair a healthcare executive with a genetics PhD, and pharma partnerships (Sanofi, Cytiva) validate the platform. The long gap between rounds and strong rivals like Dyno are the main risks.
notes: Series A dated 2022-09 by TechCrunch and databases; Jones Day page dates its post 2022-07 for the Omnes led 10M financing, a possible earlier close. Amount reported in USD by TechCrunch and Newswire (some databases give 9.8M to 10.0M euros). Series B: Pulse2 and HLTH both report 26M; HLTH labeled it Series B and one other outlet called it Series A+, treated as less reliable. Total equity funding may be incomplete (grants, French public funding not checked). Outcome search found no layoffs or acquisition. Competitor sources: TechCrunch article dated 2022-09, after the Winter 2022 batch start.
